title: Instability of Gaussian elimination is exponentially rare (proof of partial result)
summary: Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting is the standard algorithm for solving a dense $n\times n$ system of linear equations $Ax=b$. The ``growth factor'' $ρ\,$ for this process may be as large as $2^{n-1}$, and when $ρ$ is large, the algorithm is unstable. Nevertheless, long experience has shown that Gaussian elimination is resoundingly stable in practice. Experiments indicate that among random matrices with independent normally distributed entries, growth factors $ρ\gg n^{1/2}$ are in a precise sense exponentially rare.
